```{python}
#| output: false
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import requests
import xgboost as xgb
from pathlib import Path
from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_line, geom_point, geom_histogram, labs, theme_minimal,
)
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import HTML, display
from sportsdataverse.nfl import load_nfl_schedule, load_nfl_teams

def _fetch(url, timeout=600):
    """Fetch bytes, refusing to return a non-200 body.

    Without raise_for_status a 404/500 HTML error page is written under a
    .parquet/.ubj filename, and every later run treats it as valid because only
    file EXISTENCE is checked -- a poisoned cache and a silently wrong document.
    """
    r = requests.get(url, timeout=timeout)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.content

ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "docs" / "models").is_dir() or not (ROOT / "models").is_dir():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
CACHE = ROOT / "docs" / "models" / ".cache"
CACHE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
fd_path = CACHE / "fd_model.ubj"
if not fd_path.exists():
    fd_path.write_bytes(_fetch(
        "https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download/nfl_4th_down_models/fd_model.ubj",
        timeout=600))
bst = xgb.Booster()
bst.load_model(str(fd_path))
pbp_path = CACHE / "model_pbp_2025.parquet"
if not pbp_path.exists():
    pbp_path.write_bytes(_fetch(
        "https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download/nfl_model_pbp/model_pbp_2025.parquet",
        timeout=600))
pbp = pl.read_parquet(pbp_path)

def gt_show(g):
    display(HTML(g.as_raw_html()))


```

The fourth-down yards model predicts the **distribution of yards gained** on a
go-for-it (or third-down) attempt — the core of the **nfl4th** decision surface.
From the 76-class gain distribution we derive P(first down) for any
distance-to-go, then combine it with the EP/WP surfaces to compute the
**go / punt / field-goal / two-point** expected-value comparison. It is a
faithful Python retrain of nfl4th's go-for-it model, validated against the
converted nflverse artifact.

This document is compiled: the conversion-probability curve is derived from the
released booster at render time (summing class probabilities over the
distance-to-go), and compared with the latest published season's **empirical**
4th-down conversion rates.

## Model features

**14 features**; one row per 3rd/4th-down scrimmage play (1999–2025, `qb_kneel==0`,
`week<=17`). The label is `yards_gained` clamped to **[−10, 65]** and shifted into
**76 ordinal classes** (`label = yards_gained + 10`).

| Feature | Type | What it encodes |
|---|---|---|
| `down` | numeric | Current down (3 or 4). |
| `ydstogo` | numeric | Yards to go — the conversion threshold. |
| `yardline_100` | numeric | Field position (compresses the gain distribution near the goal line). |
| `era0`..`era4` | one-hot | Rule-era one-hot (cuts 2001/2005/2013/2017) — era-aware across 1999–2025. |
| `outdoors` / `retractable` / `dome` | binary | Stadium-type one-hots. |
| `posteam_spread` | numeric | Possession-team spread (game-script context). |
| `total_line` | numeric | Game total (pace / offensive-environment proxy). |
| `posteam_total` | numeric | Possession-team implied total. |

## The model

**Algorithm.** XGBoost, `objective=multi:softprob` over **76 classes**, **1,124
rounds**, `eta=0.01`, `max_depth=2`, `gamma=2`, `subsample=0.8`,
`colsample_bytree=0.8`, `min_child_weight=0.8` — verbatim from the nfl4th R recipe.
P(first down) for any distance-to-go is recovered by summing class probabilities
for gains ≥ the distance.

**Evaluation.** Parity against the converted nflverse artifact: **mean-gain
correlation 0.9856** (informational — era-aware full-history retrain vs the
nfl4th 2014–19 oracle) — see [Parity](parity.md).

## P(convert) vs reality, render time

```{python}
#| output: false
feats = bst.feature_names
grid = pl.DataFrame({"ydstogo": np.arange(1, 16)}).with_columns(
    pl.lit(4.0).alias("down"), pl.lit(55.0).alias("yardline_100"),
    pl.lit(0).alias("era0"), pl.lit(0).alias("era1"), pl.lit(0).alias("era2"),
    pl.lit(0).alias("era3"), pl.lit(1).alias("era4"),
    pl.lit(1).alias("outdoors"), pl.lit(0).alias("retractable"), pl.lit(0).alias("dome"),
    pl.lit(0.0).alias("posteam_spread"), pl.lit(44.5).alias("total_line"),
    pl.lit(22.25).alias("posteam_total"),
)
X = grid.select(feats).to_numpy().astype(np.float32)
probs = bst.predict(xgb.DMatrix(X, feature_names=feats))
if probs.ndim == 1:
    probs = probs.reshape(len(grid), -1)
# class k = yards_gained k-10; conversion iff yards_gained >= ydstogo
p_conv = []
for i, ytg in enumerate(grid["ydstogo"].to_list()):
    k0 = int(ytg + 10)
    p_conv.append(float(probs[i, k0:].sum()))
model_curve = pl.DataFrame({"ydstogo": grid["ydstogo"], "p": p_conv,
                            "series": ["model P(convert)"] * len(p_conv)})
go = pbp.filter((pl.col("down") == 4) & pl.col("play_type").is_in(["pass", "run"])
                & (pl.col("ydstogo") <= 15))
emp = (
    go.group_by("ydstogo")
    .agg((pl.col("yards_gained") >= pl.col("ydstogo")).mean().alias("p"), pl.len().alias("n"))
    .filter(pl.col("n") >= 15)
    .with_columns(pl.lit("empirical 2025 (attempts)").alias("series"))
    .select("ydstogo", "p", "series")
)
curve = pl.concat([model_curve, emp])
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Model P(convert) at midfield (neutral spread, era4) vs realized 2025 4th-down conversion rates — selection effects push the empirical curve above the unconditional model."
(
    ggplot(curve.to_pandas(), aes("ydstogo", "p", color="series"))
    + geom_line() + geom_point(alpha=0.7)
    + labs(x="yards to go", y="P(convert)",
           title=f"4th-down conversion — model vs 2025 attempts ({go.height} gos)")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

Teams *choose* which 4th downs to attempt, so the realized curve reflects
selection while the model curve is the unconditional estimate at a fixed neutral
state — the gap between them is selection, not error. That distinction is the
whole reason the decision layer values options with a model rather than
empirical rates.

**What the selection actually is** was measured separately over 42,454 fourth
downs, 2014–2025 REG (7,501 go attempts), and it is not the intuitive story.
Coaches are *not* mainly going when they like the matchup: goers and non-goers
differ by −0.60 SD on score differential and −0.57 SD on time remaining, but only
−0.13 SD on market-implied team quality. **Selection is on game state, not on who
is playing.** The pooled conversion gap is +11.6 pp, but it is compositional —
within matched distance and field-position cells the gap *flips negative* (to
−0.14 in the 3–5 and 6–10 yard cells). So the empirical curve sitting above the
model is a mix effect, not evidence that attempted 4th downs are easier than the
model thinks; conditioning on distance removes it and then some. Full method and
numbers: `ClaudeCowork/notes/2026-09-02-odds-dispersion-and-postgame-we/`.

## The decision surface in use — 2025

The published pbp carries the nfl4th-style decision columns (`go_wp_diff`,
`fg_wp_diff`, `punt_wp_diff`) plus `fourth_down_recommendation`.

**Read the `*_wp_diff` columns carefully**: each is that option's WP *minus the
best option's*, so every one of them is `<= 0` and the recommended option is the
one sitting at exactly `0`. A `go_wp_diff > 0` test is therefore always false —
it is never satisfied on any play in any season — and a table built on it
silently reports "the model never says go" plus an agreement rate that is really
just the share of 4th downs teams did not go for. This document made that
mistake until 2026-09-01. The unambiguous column is
`fourth_down_recommendation`, which matches `go_wp_diff == 0` exactly (2025:
2,004 of 2,004; 2024: 1,860 of 1,860), so it is what the tables below use.

```{python}
dec = pbp.filter((pl.col("down") == 4) & pl.col("fourth_down_recommendation").is_not_null())
dec = dec.with_columns(
    pl.col("play_type").is_in(["pass", "run"]).fill_null(False).alias("went"),
    (pl.col("fourth_down_recommendation") == "go").alias("should_go"),
)
gt_show(
    GT(pl.DataFrame({
        "check": ["4th downs with a recommendation", "model says GO",
                  "teams actually went", "went WHEN the model says go",
                  "went when the model says kick", "coach–model agreement rate"],
        "value": [float(dec.height), float(dec["should_go"].sum()), float(dec["went"].sum()),
                  float(dec.filter(pl.col("should_go"))["went"].mean()),
                  float(dec.filter(~pl.col("should_go"))["went"].mean()),
                  float((dec["went"] == dec["should_go"]).mean())],
    }).to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Decision layer vs coaches — 2025 season",
                subtitle="the model recommends going on ~47% of 4th downs; teams go on ~21%")
    .fmt_number(columns="value", decimals=3)
)
```

## Coach-indexed decision calibration, 2021–2025

League-wide agreement hides the thing the decision surface is actually used to
argue about, which is that coaches differ. Indexing by the coach on the sideline
(from the schedule's `home_coach` / `away_coach`, assigned to whichever side had
the ball) turns one number into a distribution:

```{python}
#| output: false
YEARS = [2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025]
frames = []
for season in YEARS:
    path = CACHE / f"model_pbp_{season}.parquet"
    if not path.exists():
        path.write_bytes(_fetch(
            f"https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download/nfl_model_pbp/model_pbp_{season}.parquet",
            timeout=600))
    frames.append(
        pl.read_parquet(path)
        .filter((pl.col("down") == 4) & pl.col("fourth_down_recommendation").is_not_null())
        .select("game_id", "season", "posteam", "home_team", "play_type",
                "fourth_down_recommendation", "go_boost")
    )
multi = pl.concat(frames, how="vertical_relaxed")

sched = load_nfl_schedule(YEARS).select("game_id", "home_coach", "away_coach")
teams = load_nfl_teams().select("team_abbr", "team_logo_espn")
multi = multi.join(sched, on="game_id", how="left").with_columns(
    pl.when(pl.col("posteam") == pl.col("home_team")).then(pl.col("home_coach"))
      .otherwise(pl.col("away_coach")).alias("coach"),
    pl.col("play_type").is_in(["pass", "run"]).fill_null(False).alias("went"),
    (pl.col("fourth_down_recommendation") == "go").alias("should_go"),
).filter(pl.col("coach").is_not_null())

coaches = (
    multi.group_by("coach").agg(
        pl.len().alias("decisions"),
        pl.col("posteam").last().alias("team"),
        pl.col("should_go").mean().alias("model_go_rate"),
        pl.col("went").mean().alias("actual_go_rate"),
        pl.col("should_go").sum().alias("n_should"),
        pl.col("went").filter(pl.col("should_go")).mean().alias("go_when_should"),
        pl.col("went").filter(~pl.col("should_go")).mean().alias("go_when_kick"),
        # go_boost is the WP gain (percentage points) the model attributes to
        # going; summed over the recommended-go plays a coach kicked away, it is
        # the WP that decision cost him.
        pl.col("go_boost").filter(pl.col("should_go") & ~pl.col("went")).sum().alias("wp_forgone"),
    )
    .filter(pl.col("decisions") >= 150)
    .with_columns((pl.col("wp_forgone") / pl.col("decisions")).alias("wp_forgone_per_decision"))
    .join(teams, left_on="team", right_on="team_abbr", how="left")
    .with_columns(("<img src='" + pl.col("team_logo_espn").fill_null("") + "' height='26' alt=''/>").alias("logo"))
    .sort("go_when_should", descending=True)
)
league_go_when_should = float(multi.filter(pl.col("should_go"))["went"].mean())

# Wilson 95% score interval on go_when_should. A range of point estimates says
# nothing on its own -- the smallest displayed group has ~150 decisions, so the
# question is whether the spread survives sampling variation. Wilson rather than
# normal-approximation because these are proportions near the tails on modest n.
_Z = 1.959963984540054  # exact two-sided 95% normal quantile, not the 1.96 shorthand
coaches = coaches.with_columns(
    (
        (pl.col("go_when_should") + _Z**2 / (2 * pl.col("n_should"))
         - _Z * ((pl.col("go_when_should") * (1 - pl.col("go_when_should")) / pl.col("n_should")
                  + _Z**2 / (4 * pl.col("n_should") ** 2)).sqrt()))
        / (1 + _Z**2 / pl.col("n_should"))
    ).alias("gws_lo"),
    (
        (pl.col("go_when_should") + _Z**2 / (2 * pl.col("n_should"))
         + _Z * ((pl.col("go_when_should") * (1 - pl.col("go_when_should")) / pl.col("n_should")
                  + _Z**2 / (4 * pl.col("n_should") ** 2)).sqrt()))
        / (1 + _Z**2 / pl.col("n_should"))
    ).alias("gws_hi"),
)
_top, _bot = coaches.row(0, named=True), coaches.row(coaches.height - 1, named=True)
_disjoint = _top["gws_lo"] > _bot["gws_hi"]

# Wilson answers "are the two extremes separable?". It does not answer "how much
# of the SPREAD is real?" -- for that, split the observed between-coach variance
# into true and sampling parts. Note the >=150 cut is on `decisions` (all fourth
# downs) while the ranking is on a rate denominated in `n_should`, a median of
# roughly half that, so the cut does not bound the ranking's noise.
_var_obs = float(coaches["go_when_should"].var())
_pbar = league_go_when_should
_var_noise = float((_pbar * (1 - _pbar) / coaches["n_should"]).mean())
_var_true = max(_var_obs - _var_noise, 0.0)
_reliability = _var_true / _var_obs if _var_obs else 0.0
# empirical-Bayes shrinkage toward the league rate, weight = true/(true+noise)
_shr = coaches.with_columns(
    (_var_true / (_var_true + _pbar * (1 - _pbar) / pl.col("n_should"))).alias("w")
).with_columns((_pbar + pl.col("w") * (pl.col("go_when_should") - _pbar)).alias("p_shrunk"))
_rng_raw = float(coaches["go_when_should"].max() - coaches["go_when_should"].min())
_rng_shr = float(_shr["p_shrunk"].max() - _shr["p_shrunk"].min())
_ratio_raw = float(coaches["go_when_should"].max() / coaches["go_when_should"].min())
_ratio_shr = float(_shr["p_shrunk"].max() / _shr["p_shrunk"].min())
_nsh_med, _dec_med = int(coaches["n_should"].median()), int(coaches["decisions"].median())
_churn = int(_shr.with_columns(
    pl.col("go_when_should").rank(descending=True).alias("a"),
    pl.col("p_shrunk").rank(descending=True).alias("b"),
).filter((pl.col("a") - pl.col("b")).abs() >= 5).height)
_max_shrunk = float(_shr["p_shrunk"].max())
```

```{python}
show = pl.concat([coaches.head(8), coaches.tail(8)])
gt_show(
    GT(show.select("logo", "coach", "decisions", "model_go_rate", "actual_go_rate",
                   "go_when_should", "go_when_kick", "wp_forgone_per_decision").to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Aggressiveness on 4th down by head coach — 2021–2025",
                subtitle=f"top 8 and bottom 8 of {coaches.height} coaches with >=150 decisions; "
                         f"league go-rate when the model says go is {league_go_when_should:.1%}")
    .fmt_markdown(columns="logo")
    .fmt_percent(columns=["model_go_rate", "actual_go_rate", "go_when_should", "go_when_kick"], decimals=1)
    .fmt_number(columns="wp_forgone_per_decision", decimals=3)
    .cols_label(logo="", coach="Coach", decisions="Dec", model_go_rate="Model go%",
                actual_go_rate="Actual go%", go_when_should="Go when told",
                go_when_kick="Go when told to kick", wp_forgone_per_decision="WP pts left / dec")
)
```

Three things this makes visible that the league-wide number cannot:

- **The spread is large, and it survives sampling variation.** Go-rate-when-the-
  model-says-go runs from 25% to 50% across coaches — the most aggressive coach
  in the sample goes twice as often as the most conservative *in the same
  recommended situations*. A range of point estimates alone would not establish
  that, so the extremes carry Wilson 95% intervals:
  `{python} f"{_top['coach']} {_top['go_when_should']:.1%} [{_top['gws_lo']:.1%}, {_top['gws_hi']:.1%}] on n={int(_top['n_should'])}"`
  versus
  `{python} f"{_bot['coach']} {_bot['go_when_should']:.1%} [{_bot['gws_lo']:.1%}, {_bot['gws_hi']:.1%}] on n={int(_bot['n_should'])}"`
  — `{python} "disjoint, so the gap is not sampling noise" if _disjoint else "OVERLAPPING, so the extremes are not separable at 95% and the range should be read as observed spread only"`.
  Separability is not the same question as magnitude, though, and the raw range
  overstates the magnitude. The `>=150` cut is on `decisions`, while the ranked
  rate is denominated in recommended-go plays — a median of
  `{python} f"{_nsh_med}"` against `{python} f"{_dec_med}"` — so the cut never
  bounded the ranking's noise. Splitting the between-coach variance into true and
  sampling parts puts reliability at `{python} f"{_reliability:.2f}"`, i.e.
  `{python} f"{(1-_reliability)*100:.0f}"`% of the visible spread is sampling
  error. Shrinking each coach toward the league rate by his own precision narrows
  the range from `{python} f"{_rng_raw*100:.1f}"` pp to
  `{python} f"{_rng_shr*100:.1f}"` pp and the "twice as often" ratio to
  `{python} f"{_ratio_shr:.1f}"`×. **Both readings are true: the spread is real
  (Wilson) and smaller than it looks (shrinkage) — quote the shrunk range.** The
  *ordering* is durable: `{python} f"{_churn}"` coaches move five or more places
  under shrinkage.
- **Every coach is conservative relative to the model**, and this survives
  shrinkage — the most aggressive coach's shrunk rate is
  `{python} f"{_max_shrunk:.1%}"`. Even the top of the
  table converts only half of the model's go recommendations. The gap is
  systematic, not a handful of outliers, which is the honest reading: either
  coaches price in things the model cannot see (personnel, weather, injury,
  job security) or the model's go branch is optimistic. This document cannot
  separate those two.
- **`model_go_rate` differs by coach too**, which is a *situation* effect, not a
  tendency one — a coach whose team trails often faces more go-recommended 4th
  downs. Read `go_when_should` (a rate *within* recommended situations), not
  `actual_go_rate`, when comparing coaches.

The WP column is deliberately the *per-decision* average rather than a season
total, so a coach with 659 decisions is not penalised against one with 154 for
merely having coached more games.

## Decision surface

`fd_model` is one input to nfl4th's 4th-down EV comparison; the others are
[`fg_model`](fg.md), [`two_pt_model`](two_pt.md), the [punt distribution](punt.md),
and the [nfl4th home-WP](nfl4th_wp.md). Each option's EV is computed by mapping its
outcome distribution through the WP surface and picking the highest-WP action.

## Limitations

The label is recorded `yards_gained`, which can disagree with the official result
on penalty/lateral plays — label noise at the tails. The gain window is clipped
to [−10, 65]. It predicts a *yardage distribution*, not the binary decision; the
decision EV is computed downstream.

**The recommendation is a point estimate with no interval, and the interval is
wide.** Split-conformal prediction sets at 90% over the same 2014–2025 sample
achieve 0.892 empirical coverage (CI [0.876, 0.907], clustered by game — the
calibration is honest), but at that confidence **64.3% of go attempts are
uncallable**: the prediction set contains both outcomes, so the model cannot
distinguish convert from fail for roughly two thirds of the attempts it scores.
Treat `fourth_down_recommendation` as a decision rule under uncertainty, not as a
claim about what will happen on the play. This does not impugn the EV comparison
— an EV rule is still correct on average when each individual call is uncertain —
but it does bound how much weight a single flagged decision can carry.

## Avenues for improvement & open issues

- **Resolved (2026-09-01, PR #29):** *Coach-level tendencies* — decision
  calibration is now indexed by head coach (2021–2025, 42 coaches with >=150
  decisions). Go-rate within model-recommended situations spans 25%–50% against
  a 36% league rate, and every coach in the sample sits below the model.
- **Resolved (2026-09-01, PR #29):** the decision table's `go_wp_diff > 0` test
  was never satisfiable — the `*_wp_diff` columns are differences against the
  best option, so they are always `<= 0`. It now reads
  `fourth_down_recommendation`.
- **Whether the residual gap is coaches or the model** got narrower on one side
  (2026-09-02): "coaches price in unobservables" needs those unobservables to
  correlate with the go decision, and measured selection is on game state
  (−0.60 SD score differential) and barely on team quality (−0.13 SD) — a
  *situational* rule rather than a matchup read. That weakens, without
  eliminating, the unobservables story. It is still not settled here.
  Every coach being conservative relative to the surface is equally consistent
  with coaches pricing in unobservables and with the go branch being optimistic;
  separating them needs a holdout on realized outcomes, not more slicing.
- **Known issue:** the 76-class yards head shares the xYAC machinery — the
  multiclass pred_contribs 3-D gotcha applies to any explainability pass.
